acceptance_tests.scenario: every authoritative connection path uses ConnectionFactory
FK-to-index analyser over complete release schema

acceptance_tests.scenario: clean initialization and every supported migration origin
prove: clean-init temp database is never published before full verification
retry applies each accepted migration exactly once
runtime never rewrites manifest or ledger to match unexpected bytes
current offline target bytes/mtime are unchanged
unsafe offline sidecar state returns limited classification without touching writer
domain mutation + required lifecycle event + command receipt + audit all commit or all rollback
OR IGNORE/REPLACE is absent from audit repository
historical payload version remains readable without rewrite
duplicate keys/NaN/Infinity/malformed UTF-8/unknown version follow contract

acceptance_tests.scenario: two concurrent launches against same data instance
prove: second never migrates or binds competing authoritative host
verified-existing-instance path is used or second exits safely
socket is pre-bound before Uvicorn receives it
registry mismatch never causes unrelated shutdown
registry is removed only for exact current run/data identity
same command_id + same request_hash returns prior result with no duplicate audit/event
same command_id + different hash fails integrity
BEGIN IMMEDIATE contention returns retryable busy rather than partial write
no write transaction includes artificial wait/operator/file parsing

acceptance_tests.scenario: graceful shutdown under idle and active work
prove: WAL checkpoint/connection close/socket close/lock release occur in order
new clean instance gets one stable data_instance_id
restart/path display changes do not change it
new empty instance never reuses prior identity
Starlette/Uvicorn direct dependency set imports and executes startup/shutdown on both supported Python lines
no installed Node.js is needed at runtime
fresh preconditions prove requested state already equals accepted target state
no domain row/revision/lifecycle event/audit event is fabricated
lost-response retry with same command_id/hash returns NO_CHANGE even if unrelated state later changes
same command_id with different hash still fails integrity
